title: MEDALLION: Manifold Embedding Distillation and Attributions for Low-dimensional Latent InterpretatiON
abstract: arXiv:2611.08767v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Dimensionality reduction is widely used to visualize high-dimensional data and guide scientific discovery, yet interpreting which original features contribute to low-dimensional representations remains challenging, particularly for black-box methods such as t-SNE and UMAP. We introduce \textbf{MEDALLION} (Manifold Embedding Distillation and Attributions for Low-dimensional Latent InterpretatiON), a novel framework for interpreting low-dimensional embeddings through knowledge distillation and neural feature attribution. MEDALLION distills any given embedding with a neural encoder which we explain via a broad range of existing neural feature attribution methods. Through experiments on MNIST and applications in single-cell transcriptomics, we show MEDALLION provides informative feature attributions that cast additional insights into the underlying embedding and compare its performance with existing interpretability approaches.

translated_title: MEDALLION：用于低维潜在解释的流形嵌入蒸馏与归因
translated_abstract: 降维被广泛用于高维数据可视化和科学发现指导，然而解释哪些原始特征对低维表征有贡献仍然具有挑战性，尤其是对于t-SNE和UMAP等黑盒方法。我们提出了MEDALLION（Manifold Embedding Distillation and Attributions for Low-dimensional Latent InterpretatiON），这是一个通过知识蒸馏和神经特征归因来解释低维嵌入的新型框架。MEDALLION使用神经编码器对任意给定的嵌入进行蒸馏，随后通过多种现有的神经特征归因方法对该编码器进行解释。通过在MNIST上的实验以及单细胞转录组学中的应用，我们展示了MEDALLION能够提供信息丰富的特征归因，为底层嵌入带来额外的见解，并将其性能与现有的可解释性方法进行了比较。
tldr: MEDALLION提出了一种结合知识蒸馏与神经特征归因的新框架，能够解释任意降维方法（如t-SNE、UMAP）生成的低维嵌入中哪些原始特征起关键作用。
en_tdlr: MEDALLION introduces a novel framework combining knowledge distillation and neural feature attribution to interpret which original features contribute to low-dimensional embeddings produced by any dimensionality reduction method such as t-SNE and UMAP.
